result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.select_last_edges_created()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select the last N edges that were created. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5780-L5827){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_last_edges_created(n) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Selects edges in reverse chronological order based on creation time. Useful for incremental graph building workflows where you want to work with recently added edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of most recently created edges to select. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Select recently added edges: ::: {#1f8352fa .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="D", target="E") .select_last_edges_created(n=2) ) # Last 2 edges selected count = graph.count_selected_edges() # Returns 2 count ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
